jobs.title: Relationship Executive-Healthcare, Higher Education & Nonprofit-Executive Director
jobs.description:
**JOB DESCRIPTION**  
  
  

You are customer focused, enjoy building relationships and providing financial advice to your clients. A role as a Healthcare, Higher Education, Nonprofit Commercial Banker is for you.

As a Relationship Manager you will be the focal point of client acquisition and ongoing relationships. Bankers work both independently and as part of a team to introduce our comprehensive solutions to clients. As a Banker, you will be responsible for growing and retaining profitable relationships with not-for-profit health systems, universities and colleges, and not-for-profit organizations within the Middle Market Banking & Specialized Industries. This banker will work with clients and partner across the national Healthcare, Higher Education, Nonprofit footprint - Treasury, Industry Solutions, Credit - as well other firmwide JPM resources. including Investment Banking, Derivatives, Corporate Responsibility, among others.

Our Bankers are required to have deep working knowledge of our solutions including, but not limited to: Credit, Treasury Services, International Banking, Syndicated Finance, Commercial Card and Chase Paymentech Solutions. Our strongest Bankers have a methodical approach to the market activity and prospecting. Middle Market Banking & Specialized Industries delivers locally and therefore our ideal candidate has deep local connections and market knowledge.

**Job Responsibilities**

* Champion a culture of innovation and a customer centric mindset
* Stay up to date with industry trends to identify opportunities for innovation or strategic partnerships
* Find ways to further efficiency with existing technical infrastructure through automation while embracing the innovative opportunities offered by new technologies

**Required Qualifications, Capabilities and Skills**

* 5+ years direct lending or credit support related experience with a focus on business relationships
* Understanding of Commercial Banking products and services
* Ability to mobilize internal networks and resources
* Demonstrated experience of meeting or exceeding sales goals
* Excellent organizational skills and the ability to manage, prioritize, work under pressure and meet tight deadlines
* Excellent verbal and written communications skills; able to effectively communicate clearly and concisely
* Strong interpersonal and influencing skills, with the ability to establish credibility and strong partnership with senior business and control partners

**Preferred Qualifications, Capabilities and Skills**

* Bachelor's degree and formal credit training preferred
* Sales management, business development skills, proficiency in building and maintaining positive client relationships
* Strong creative solution, problem solving abilities, flexible to changing business priorities and ability to multitask
* Excellent business judgment, strategic thinking, self-directed, proactive and creative

**ABOUT US**  
  
  

JPMorganChase, one of the oldest financial institutions, offers innovative financial solutions to millions of consumers, small businesses and many of the world's most prominent corporate, institutional and government clients under the J.P. Morgan and Chase brands. Our history spans over 200 years and today we are a leader in investment banking, consumer and small business banking, commercial banking, financial transaction processing and asset management.

We offer a competitive total rewards package including base salary determined based on the role, experience, skill set and location. Those in eligible roles may receive commission-based pay and/or discretionary incentive compensation, paid in the form of cash and/or forfeitable equity, awarded in recognition of individual achievements and contributions. We also offer a range of benefits and programs to meet employee needs, based on eligibility. These benefits include comprehensive health care coverage, on-site health and wellness centers, a retirement savings plan, backup childcare, tuition reimbursement, mental health support, financial coaching and more. Additional details about total compensation and benefits will be provided during the hiring process.

We recognize that our people are our strength and the diverse talents they bring to our global workforce are directly linked to our success. We are an equal opportunity employer and place a high value on diversity and inclusion at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of any protected attribute, including race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, marital or veteran status, pregnancy or disability, or any other basis protected under applicable law. We also make reasonable accommodations for applicants' and employees' religious practices and beliefs, as well as mental health or physical disability needs. Visit our FAQs for more information about requesting an accommodation.

JPMorgan Chase & Co. is an Equal Opportunity Employer, including Disability/Veterans

  
  
**ABOUT THE TEAM**  
  
  

J.P. Morgan's Global Banking business is one of the largest wholesale banking client franchises in the world. We serve clients, including corporations, governments, states, municipalities, healthcare organizations, education institutions, banks and investors.  
  
Global Investment Banking supports a broad range of corporations, institutions and governments by providing strategic advice, capital raising and risk management expertise.

jobs.description:

This is a senior leadership role within JPMorganChase's Card business that requires technical depth in AI/ML, the ability to translate between business strategy and technical execution, and a track record of building high-performing analytics teams.

As the Head of Card Customer Analytics & AI Enablement leading the Card Customer & Strategic Analytics team, you'll lead a group of analytics leaders, data scientists, and analysts responsible for delivering AI and analytics solutions that shape product strategy, customer experience, and competitive positioning across the Card portfolio. Your role will span three core areas: setting AI and analytical direction across multiple business domains, serving as the bridge between senior business stakeholders and technical teams, and building organizational capability through talent development, inclusive culture, and operational excellence.

**Job Responsibilities**

* Define and drive the AI and analytics strategy for Card D&A, identifying high-value opportunities for generative AI, agentic AI, and advanced analytics to create competitive advantage
* Stay current on emerging AI/ML techniques and evaluate new capabilities, tools, and vendor offerings for practical application in the Card business
* Partner with Data, Product, Technology, Risk, and Finance to deliver AI and ML solutions from ideation through production deployment, ensuring solutions are scalable, responsible, and aligned to business needs
* Lead analytics supporting customer experience, benefits, product design, portfolio performance, and pricing and targeting strategies

* Champion a culture of innovation, intellectual rigor, inclusion, and collaborative problem-solving across the broader Card Data & Analytics organization

**Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills**

* Master's or PhD in a quantitative field and 10+ years of progressive analytics experience
* Senior leadership experience managing and developing multi-disciplinary analytics teams, including managers and individual contributors with strong coaching, org design, and talent development skills
* Strong technical foundation in AI/ML, including experience evaluating and adopting emerging techniques, guiding architecture decisions, and moving solutions from prototype to production

* Experience with causal inference, A/B testing, and experimentation frameworks at scale

* Experience in Card, consumer lending, or payments analytics, including familiarity with installment products, credit risk, or customer lifecycle management
* Experience building or leading competitive intelligence functions using alternative data, market data, or external benchmarking

jobs.title: Executive Director, Product - Agentic Identity
jobs.description:
**JOB DESCRIPTION**  
  
  

Help shape how customers safely use AI-powered agents to act on their behalf. In this role, you will build the product strategy and platform direction for trusted, auditable agent identity and delegated authorization across digital channels.

Job summary

As a **executive director product agentic identity** in **Trust and security**, you define the framework for recognizing, identifying, and permissioning agents that act on behalf of customers across end-to-end journeys. You align standards, controls, and operating model decisions across stakeholders and partner closely with technology teams to deliver core platform capabilities. You drive measurable outcomes that improve security, traceability, and customer experience while enabling new digital experiences at scale.

Job responsibilities

* Define the product vision and enterprise framework for agent identity, authentication, and authorization, including policy, experience principles, and control requirements.
* Set the strategy for delegated authorization that scales across use cases and channels, including both firm-managed and third-party agent ecosystems.
* Own a multi-year roadmap that balances near-term delivery with longer-term interoperability and ecosystem readiness (for example, verifiable credentials).
* Define how delegation records are represented and governed, including consent, scope, assurance level, revocation, and audit artifacts.
* Create and maintain a permissions taxonomy and tiering model to enforce least-privilege access for agent actions.
* Partner with legal, compliance, and risk stakeholders to ensure customer consent and data access controls meet regulatory and internal policy expectations.
* Partner with engineering to build and extend authorization infrastructure, including tokens and enforcement tied to customer identity, agent identity, scopes, delegation identifiers, and assurance levels.
* Define requirements for step-up authentication and human-in-the-loop patterns for higher-risk actions initiated by agents.
* Drive requirements for agent registration and governance capabilities, including identity metadata, keys, and platform attributes aligned to a scalable trust model.
* Partner with fraud and analytics teams to define agent-specific monitoring and behavioral analytics needs, ensuring the platform provides telemetry and auditability for investigations and control testing.
* Establish governance and operating rhythms, including decision forums, intake, prioritization, and dependency management across identity and channel roadmaps.

Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills

* Extensive product leadership experience owning strategy, roadmap, and outcomes across multiple teams and dependencies.
* Strong understanding of identity and access management patterns, including delegated authorization, assurance levels, and step-up authentication.
* Working knowledge of modern authorization standards such as OAuth (open authorization) and OpenID Connect, and the ability to translate them into clear product requirements.
* Demonstrated ability to partner with technology teams to deliver platform capabilities, including requirements, prioritization, and milestone execution.
* Experience designing durable consent and authorization models with strong auditability, revocation, and traceability.
* Strong risk and controls mindset, with experience embedding control requirements into product delivery.
* Ability to collaborate effectively with legal, compliance, risk, fraud, and analytics partners on customer-impacting capabilities.
* Strong systems thinking across channels, application programming interfaces, and enforcement layers.
* Strong analytical skills to define success metrics and use data to guide tradeoffs and prioritization.
* Excellent communication skills, including producing clear product documentation and aligning technical and non-technical audiences.

Preferred qualifications, capabilities, and skills

* Experience delivering identity and authorization capabilities in regulated financial services environments.
* Experience with verifiable credentials and cross-organization trust models.
* Experience defining tiered permissions models and least-privilege approaches for high-risk actions.
* Familiarity with fraud detection, monitoring signals, and investigation workflows for digital channels.

Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the US. We are not able to provide immigration sponsorship or take over sponsorship of an employment visa at this time. Final job grade level and corporate title will be determined at time of offer and may differ from this posting.

jobs.title: Director of Advancement
jobs.description:
**Position: Director of Advancement**

**Department:** Advancement  
**Reports to:** Chief Advancement Officer

**Position Summary**

The Director of Advancement reports to and serves as a senior strategic partner for the Chief Advancement Officer, providing high-level coordination, analysis, and execution support to advance PAL’s fundraising, campaign, and Board engagement priorities.

This role is designed to strengthen organizational alignment, accountability, and momentum during a period of growth and transition. The Director works closely with the Advancement team and across functional areas to ensure that major initiatives, campaigns, and donor strategies are effectively planned, resourced, and executed.

The ideal candidate is a trusted advisor with strong organizational judgment, exceptional project management skills, and the ability to operate seamlessly at the intersection of strategy, governance, and execution.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Strategic Planning & Campaign Coordination**

* Partner with the CAO to develop, execute, and monitor multi-year fundraising and campaign strategies.
* Coordinate major campaign timelines, priorities, and deliverables.
* Support the development of comprehensive donor cultivation and solicitation plans.
* Track progress toward revenue and engagement goals and recommend course corrections.

**Communications Strategy**

* Support overall communications strategy and goals, driving content and execution on stakeholder engagement.
* Oversee social media strategy, website, email engagement, and a timeline of deliverables.
* Prepare materials, briefings, and reports for the Executive Team.
* Oversee the timeline and collateral built around PAL events, accountable for the production and send of newsletters, direct mail, and campaign materials.

**Donor & Relationship Strategy**

* Support the CAO in preparing for major donor meetings, solicitations, and stewardship.
* Conduct high-level prospect analysis and strategy development.
* Coordinate follow-up and accountability for key donor relationships.

**Organizational Alignment & Accountability**

* Lead cross-departmental coordination related to Advancement priorities.
* Monitor execution of strategic initiatives and ensure timely completion.
* Develop dashboards and performance reports to support data-informed decision making.
* Support change management and continuous improvement efforts.

**Special Projects & Initiatives**

* Lead high-priority initiatives as assigned by the CAO.
* Support capital campaigns, major partnerships, and organizational growth initiatives.
* Provide analytical and operational support to complex projects.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree required; Master’s degree preferred.
* Minimum of 10 years of progressive leadership experience in nonprofit management, advancement, strategy, or executive administration.
* Demonstrated experience supporting senior executives and campaigns.
* Strong project management and organizational skills.
* Exceptional written and verbal communication abilities.
* Ability to manage multiple complex priorities with discretion and professionalism.
* High level of judgment, integrity, and collaborative leadership style.
* Experience working in complex, multi-stakeholder organizations preferred.
* Commitment to PAL’s mission and values.

jobs.title: Program Director
jobs.description:
New Destiny’s mission is to end the cycle of domestic violence and homelessness for low-income families and individuals by developing and connecting them to safe, permanent, affordable housing and services. To achieve its mission, New Destiny builds and manages housing with on-site services; offers innovative programs that assist survivors in finding and retaining affordable housing; and works to expand access to permanent housing resources for survivors. New Destiny is the largest provider of supportive housing for domestic violence survivors in New York and is a leading advocate in the effort to obtain the resources needed to end family homelessness in New York City.

**General Description**

New Destiny is seeking to hire a full-time Program Director to provide regular on-site services at two supportive housing locations in The Bronx. This role ensures consistent, trauma-informed practice in case management, crisis intervention, and community organizing, while supervising staff and coordinating with external partners. This is a full-time position

requiring one late night a week (e.g., 11:00 am to 7:00 pm). The Program Director will report directly to the Regional Director.

**Responsibilities**

**Tenant Engagement and Community Organizing:**

* Build a team to actively engage tenants to participate in program services and activities.

* Foster tenant interaction and build community within the building. In doing so, develop and implement

workshops that reflect the interests of tenants.

* Work collaboratively with colleagues to plan enriching activities for children and adults.

* Maintain transparency with tenants regarding expectations, requirements and provide support as needed.

* Build relationships with local community organizations, legal aid, healthcare providers, employment services, etc. in order to bring programming and referral sources to the tenants.

**Supervision of Case Management Services:**

* Supervise case managers at both sites, provide guidance on survivor-centered trauma-informed care.

* Split time between both sites to supervise operations, maintain visibility with staff and residents, and ensure program consistency.

* Review case files, service plans, and housing stability goals. Ensure all data entry for team is timely and accurate.

* Collaborate with Family Support Program staff at other sites to learn/share best practices and with community partners.

* Ensure team is working to mitigate rental arrears and collaborate with New Destiny’s Property Management team.

* Provide leadership, coaching, performance evaluations, staff education, and ongoing staff support.

* Oversee escalated incidents, including threats to safety and mental health crises.

**Administrative Duties:**

* Strong administrative abilities and attention to detail. Ability to adjust to the diverse needs of tenants.

* Ensure outcomes are met for funders and internal goals.

* Conduct ongoing internal monitoring and data analysis.

* Manage internal reporting for Regional Director, VP of Supportive Housing, CEO, and OTDA reporting.

* Manage and maintain relationship with property management department, mental health team and financial coaches.

**Requirements**

* Master's degree preferred in psychology, social work, or related field, bachelor’s degree required.

* A minimum of 5 years' work experience in a client-facing, nonprofit organization.

* A minimum of 3-5 years of supervisory experience in a social service setting.

* Familiarity working with survivors of domestic violence and/or homelessness.

* Must be responsible, flexible, a self-starter, able to work independently and respond appropriately to crises.

* Excellent communication and organizational skills.

* Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, teams, share point and power point.

* Experience with trauma-informed care.

**Preferred candidates will have:**

* Strong preference for Spanish fluency.

* Comprehensive knowledge of benefits, entitlements and services offered in NYC

**How to Apply**

Please visit https://newdestinyhousing.org/about-us/jobs-and-internships/ to apply for this position.

jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer
jobs.description:
With a high level of initiative, judgment, and discretion, the Cornell Cooperative Extension Sullivan County Chief Operating Officer (COO) provides leadership and oversight for assigned administrative, human resources, compliance, governance, and organizational support functions of the Association. This position serves as a senior member of the Administrative Team and works closely with the Executive Director to ensure effective administration, organizational compliance, human resource management, and operational accountability throughout the Association.  
  
The COO serves as a strategic advisor and resource to the Executive Director, management team, supervisors, Board of Directors, and Board Committees. The position provides consultation regarding employment practices, workplace law, personnel matters, risk management, organizational policy, and compliance requirements. The position exercises significant independent judgment in handling confidential and sensitive information and matters affecting the Association.  
  
This position provides oversight of administrative and operational functions through supervision and coordination of staff and systems but does not perform routine operational work directly. The COO ensures alignment of organizational practices with Cornell Cooperative Extension policies, procedures, and applicable federal, state, and local regulations.  
  
An essential component in this role is developing systems and practices that remove barriers to full inclusion in the organization’s activities and promote innovation. This position requires a skill set necessary to develop inclusive and efficient systems that impact both the internal workforce and the Association's community. This position will be responsible for a full range of management duties, including accessing confidential data and completing complex projects and reports. The COO will provide high-level leadership and oversight of IT, HR, facilities, and operations for Cornell Cooperative Extension Sullivan County.
  
  
The COO serves as staff liaison to designated Board Committees, supports governance activities, and serves as Executive Director designee or backup as assigned.

**Required Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's Degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Public Administration, Organizational Leadership, or related field. Associate's Degree and significant progressively responsible administrative experience may be considered.
* Five or more years of progressively responsible leadership experience in administration, human resources, operations oversight, or organizational management.
* Demonstrated knowledge of human resource policies, employment law, personnel administration, and organizational compliance requirements.
* Experience providing guidance and support to managers and supervisors.
* Experience handling confidential personnel matters with professionalism and discretion.
* Ability to exercise independent judgment and make sound decisions in complex situations.
* Strong leadership, organizational, project management, and problem-solving skills.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
* Ability to supervise staff and coordinate work across multiple departments.
* Ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
* Advanced proficiency with business software applications and HR information systems.
* Ability to work flexible hours, including occasional evenings and weekends, as appropriate.
* Ability to meet travel requirements associated with the position.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Knowledge of Cornell Cooperative Extension policies, procedures, and organizational structure.
* Experience working within Cornell Cooperative Extension or another nonprofit organization.
* Professional Human Resources certification (SHRM-CP, SHRM-SCP, PHR, SPHR, or equivalent).
* Experience with Workday or comparable Human Resource Information Systems.
* Experience supporting boards of directors and governance committees.

**Administrative Responsibilities:**

**Direction & Management -** **65%**

* Provide consultation and recommendations to the Executive Director and management team regarding workplace law, employment practices, personnel matters, risk management, organizational policies, and ADA/compliance requirements.
* Provide high-level, strategic planning assistance to the Executive Director in carrying out organizational operations.
* Assume the authority of the Executive Director to plan for general administrative oversight of Association operations, in the absence of the Executive Director.
* Work with Executive Director to schedule, coordinate, make arrangements for, and attend meetings and conferences, i.e., Board and Committee meetings and orientation, including agendas, minutes, reports, and other Board of Directors’ events.
* As a senior member of the Association Administrative Team, help guide the Association to research, recommend, and ensure compliance with law/system/local policies and procedures.
* Monitor and guide the effective day-to- day building operation to ensure maintenance of facilities in a safe and effective manner.
* With the Executive Director, take leadership initiative to maintain a professional work atmosphere and handle emergencies.
* Work with appropriate staff to ensure a safe working environment and an updated emergency plan for the Association.
* Provide overall administrative supervision to the Operations and HR Coordinator and Facilities Manager.
* Facilitate and manage, with Executive Director, the hiring and onboarding process, including position descriptions, Workday requisitions, required search forms, serving on search committees, performing reference checks, and issuing offer letters.
* Manage employee recruitment and retention initiatives.
* Assist in the management of conflict resolution and employee grievances.

Location: Bethesda, Maryland (Remote; Hybrid Optional)

Founded in 1971, the National Association of Community Health Centers (NACHC) serves as the leading voice for America’s Health Centers and the people and communities they serve. NACHC works to promote the provision of high-quality, affordable, community-based health care to everyone, particularly to underserved populations.

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

The Deputy Director will develop and manage all processes and systems related to the provision of training and advisory services to health centers and other clients in the areas of leadership, governance, operations, and other related areas led by the Health Center Operations and Governance (HCOG) functional area at NACHC. The Deputy Director will also support other business development and collaborate with their supervisor to identify collaboration and funding opportunities within the functional area and across NACHC’s grant and sponsor activities.

The Deputy Director must be comfortable in a fast-paced, team-based environment often requiring strategic thinking, critical analysis, solutions-orientation, data-driven efforts and successful interpersonal skills. The Deputy Director works in close coordination and collaboration with their supervisor to ensure alignment with senior leadership on vision, strategic implementation, demonstrable progress, and results.

* Collaborate with NACHC’s General Counsel on the refinement and maintenance of contract templates.
* Collaborate with NACHC’s General Counsel and Operations Functional Area to ensure NACHC maintains adequate insurance appropriate to the types of training and consultation/advisory services offered.
* Liaise with Finance on the processes for invoicing clients.
* Ensure other systems are in place for the provision of training and advisory services.

3. Manage business development and sales.

* Engage in business development and sales to secure business for the training and advisory services.

* Collaborate with HCOG Leadership, the PCA and Network Relations team, and others to frame and market services to PCAs.

* Respond to requests for services in a timely manner.
* Assemble the appropriate stakeholders to scope work.
* Develop scopes of work for training and advisory services and gain appropriate client and internal approvals.
* Develop contracts for engagements using NACHC templates and ensure each receives the client and internal NACHC approvals.
* Liaise with Finance to invoice clients for training and advisory services after an engagement is complete.

5. Manage systems and processes to ensure NACHC maintains internal and external SME trainers/consultants that are vetted and qualified to provide training and consultation/advisory services.

* Collaborate with supervisor and HCOG leadership on a process for vetting and selecting external SME trainers/consultants.
* Lead the RFP or other intake process for the provision of SME trainers/consultants in alignment with NACHC’s procurement processes.
* Collaborate with NACHC’s General Counsel on the refinement and maintenance of contracts to use with external trainers/consultants.
* Ensure all vetted and approved trainers/consultants have an agreement on file with NACHC prior to providing services.

It offers a range of products and services to meet the financial needs of its clients from retail lending, captive financing, and floorplan products to cash management, private banking, and payment processing.

* Prospect and grow commercial product offerings, with emphasis on deposit growth, and leverage the existing CS relationships to grow retail business.
* Support Private Label and original equipment manufacturer (OEM) floor plan rooftop goals.
* Manage the profitability and performance of assigned portfolio.
* Partner effectively with Merchant Services, Investment Bank, Credit Card, Private Bank and Consumer Bank to deliver the firm.
* Analyze and document the effectiveness of sales performance and results as related to KPMs.
* Serve as a subject matter expert for the regional sales team; provide mentoring, leadership, and training as needed.
* Adhere to the firm's Code of Conduct and controls/compliance.

jobs.title: Executive Director for Career Services
jobs.description:
**Executive Director for Career Services**

**Charleston Southern University**

**Position Summary**

Reporting to the Associate Vice President for Student Engagement, the Executive Director for Career Services provides strategic leadership, vision, and administrative oversight for the university's career development and workforce readiness initiatives. The Executive Director advances a comprehensive approach to career readiness that prepares students for meaningful employment, graduate education, military service, and vocational calling. Through collaboration with faculty, employers, alumni, and campus partners, the Executive Director fosters a culture of career development that supports student success, institutional priorities, workforce needs, and the university's Christian mission.

**Essential Responsibilities**

**Strategic Leadership and Administration**

* Provide visionary leadership, strategic direction, and operational oversight for all Career Services programs, services, technologies, and initiatives.
* Develop and implement a comprehensive strategic plan that advances career readiness, experiential learning, employer engagement, and post-graduation success.
* Supervise, mentor, develop, and evaluate Career Services staff while fostering a culture of collaboration, innovation, accountability, and student-centered service.
* Manage departmental budgets, resource allocation, assessment plans, and annual goals to ensure alignment with university priorities.
* Ensure compliance with university policies and applicable federal, state, and professional standards.
* Represent Career Services on university committees and serve as the university's chief advocate for career development and workforce preparation.

**Employer and External Relations**

* Lead the university's employer engagement strategy by cultivating partnerships with employers, industry leaders, graduate and professional schools, government agencies, nonprofit organizations, and community stakeholders.
* Partner with the Internship Coordinator to expand opportunities for internships, experiential learning, mentorships, cooperative education, and employment pathways for students and alumni.
* Serve as the university's primary liaison to employers, workforce development organizations, chambers of commerce, economic development agencies, and professional associations.
* Oversee employer recruiting initiatives, including career fairs, networking events, employer information sessions, on-campus interviews, and graduate/professional school programs.

**Campus Collaboration and Career Integration**

* Collaborate with academic leadership and faculty to integrate career readiness competencies throughout the curriculum and co-curricular student experience.
* Partner with colleges, academic departments, and campus stakeholders to develop discipline-specific career pathways, internship opportunities, and workforce development initiatives.
* Promote campus-wide adoption of the National Association of Colleges and Employers (NACE) Career Readiness Competencies.
* Collaborate with Student Success, Academic Affairs, Alumni Relations, Advancement, Enrollment Management, Athletics, Residence Life, and Student Engagement to embed career readiness across the student lifecycle.

**Assessment and Institutional Effectiveness**

* Provide leadership for institutional assessment strategies related to career readiness, student engagement, internship participation, first-destination outcomes, graduate school placement, and employment outcomes.
* Utilize data analytics and assessment results to improve services, demonstrate effectiveness, support accreditation efforts, and inform strategic decision-making.
* Prepare and present annual reports, performance metrics, and outcomes data to university leadership and external stakeholders.
* Provide executive oversight of career technologies and career outcomes reporting systems to ensure effective utilization and continuous improvement.

**Resource Development and Special Initiatives**

* Identify and pursue grants, sponsorships, philanthropic support, and external funding opportunities that advance Career Services initiatives.
* Provide institutional oversight and partnership support for the Federal Off-Campus Work Study Program.
* Remain informed of workforce trends, labor market developments, and emerging best practices in higher education career services to ensure continued innovation and relevance.
* Perform other duties as assigned.

**Minimum Qualifications**

**Education**

Master's degree in Higher Education Administration, Student Affairs, Counseling, Business Administration, Human Resources, Organizational Leadership, or a related field.

**Experience and Skills**

* Seven to ten years of progressively responsible experience in career services, student affairs, workforce development, higher education administration, or a related field.
* Demonstrated experience providing strategic leadership and managing complex programs, initiatives, or departments.
* Experience supervising and developing professional staff.
* Proven success in employer relations, partnership development, workforce readiness initiatives, or experiential learning programs.
* Experience with strategic planning, budgeting, assessment, and organizational effectiveness.
* Demonstrated ability to analyze and utilize data to inform decision-making and improve outcomes.
* Exceptional leadership, communication, relationship-building, and organizational skills.
* Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively with senior administrators, faculty, employers, alumni, and external stakeholders.
* Experience with career management technologies, reporting systems, and student success platforms.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience in a leadership role within a college or university career services office.
* Experience developing employer partnerships and workforce development strategies that result in measurable student outcomes.

jobs.title: Executive Director - Mental Health Client Action Network(MHCAN)
jobs.description:
**The Organization**

The Mental Health Client Action Network (MHCAN) is a non-profit 501(c)(3) organization dedicated to supporting adults in Santa Cruz County with lived experience of mental health challenges. Founded nearly 40 years ago as an independent peer support center, MHCAN is actively transitioning its operational framework to an accredited Clubhouse Model of Services.

In alignment with Clubhouse standards, MHCAN operates as a member-driven community where participants ("members") and staff work side-by-side to run daily center operations, build social connections, and pursue employment, education, and wellness goals. All MHCAN staff members share lived experience with a mental health condition and/or navigating the mental health system.

**Position Summary**

The Executive Director serves as the chief executive officer of MHCAN and is responsible for providing strategic leadership, operational oversight, program management, community engagement, and resource development. Reporting directly to the Board of Directors, the Executive Director ensures the organization stays true to its core mission of peer empowerment while successfully guiding the agency through its transition to the Clubhouse model and maintaining strong alignment with County Behavioral Health.

This is a full-time (1.0 FTE / 40 hours per week) exempt position.

**Compensation:** $95,000 – $105,000 annually, depending on experience.

**Core Responsibilities**

**Human Resources & Staff Leadership (25%)**

* Hire, train, supervise, and mentor all program staff and peer support team members.
* Foster a positive, supportive, and accountable organizational culture centered on lived experience and recovery.
* Manage staff scheduling, performance evaluations, and team development.
* Partner with the Fiscal Agent (FSAS) on HR policy enforcement, workplace safety, and personnel administration.

**Program Oversight & Clubhouse Model Transition (25%)**

* Lead the agency’s transition to and ongoing operation of a certified Clubhouse model of services.
* Ensure daily program activities effectively meet client needs and contract objectives.
* Evaluate program outcomes and implement continuous service delivery improvements.
* Monitor compliance with grant deliverables and County service agreements.

**Organizational Leadership & Strategy (20%)**

* Implement the organization's mission, vision, and strategic goals, serving as a passionate advocate for peer support.
* Develop annual organizational objectives in close collaboration with the Board of Directors and the County contract monitor.
* Ensure organizational compliance with all applicable legal and nonprofit regulatory standards.
* Provide monthly performance, operational, and financial reports to the Board.

**Community Relations & County Partnership (15%)**

* Serve as the primary spokesperson and public representative for MHCAN.
* Build and maintain productive, collaborative relationships with County Behavioral Health, local community partners, and contracted service providers.
* Represent MHCAN in local task forces, community meetings, and mental health advocacy networks.

**Fundraising & Resource Development (10%)**

* Research, write, and manage grant applications to diversify funding streams.
* Cultivate relationships with individual donors, private foundations, and community partners.
* Oversee donor stewardship and track grant reporting deadlines.

**Financial Oversight & Fiscal Agent Coordination (5%)**

* Develop and manage the annual operating budget (approximately $590,000) in partnership with the Board and Fiscal Agent.
* Collaborate directly with Front St. Administrative Services to oversee fiduciary practices, review monthly financial statements, and ensure budget alignment. *(Note: Daily bookkeeping, payroll processing, and accounting entries are performed directly by the Fiscal Agent.)*

**Qualifications**

* **Lived Experience:** Lived experience as a person with a mental health condition and/or direct experience navigating the mental health system is required.
* **Education & Experience:** Bachelor’s degree in a related field or equivalent practical experience.
* **Leadership Experience:** Minimum 2–3 years of progressively responsible leadership experience in a nonprofit or community service environment.
* **Management & Budgeting:** Demonstrated experience supervising staff, managing program operations, and overseeing grant/contract deliverables.
* **Skills:** Strong communication, interpersonal, and project management skills with the ability to build consensus across diverse community stakeholders.

**Performance Expectations**

* Maintain a balanced annual budget in coordination with the Fiscal Agent.
* Ensure successful transition and operational implementation of the Clubhouse model.
* Provide consistent leadership, accountability, and support to program staff.
* Maintain strong, transparent relationships with the Board of Directors, County Behavioral Health, and community partners.
* Ensure timely completion of grant reports and contract deliverables.

**Working Conditions & Physical Requirements**

* Standard office environment with high levels of interpersonal interaction.
* Computer and telephone usage for extended periods.
* Occasional evening or weekend attendance at Board meetings or community events.
* Local travel within Santa Cruz County.
* Ability to lift up to 25 pounds occasionally.

**Reporting Relationship:** Reports directly to the MHCAN Board of Directors.

jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer (COO)
jobs.description:
**POSITION SUMMARY**

The **Chief Operating Officer (COO)** is a key member of NCOA’s executive leadership team and a strategic partner to the President and CEO. The COO provides enterprise-wide leadership to translate NCOA’s mission, strategic priorities, and ambitious impact goals into measurable organizational results.

This is a **mission-driven, future-focused, and people-centered executive role** responsible for strengthening organizational performance and ensuring NCOA has the people, systems, technology, resources, and operating discipline needed to grow its impact. The COO leads and integrates key enterprise functions, including **People & Culture, Finance, Information Technology, and organizational operations**, while partnering across the organization to eliminate silos, strengthen accountability, and build a high-performing culture.

Equally comfortable shaping long-term strategy and addressing immediate operational challenges, the COO brings sound judgment, strong business and financial acumen, and the ability to lead through change and complexity. This leader uses data and performance measures to inform decisions, drives continuous improvement, and helps NCOA make disciplined choices about priorities, resources, and what to start, stop, scale, or strengthen.

At its core, this role is about creating the organizational conditions for NCOA to deliver on its mission: **to create the conditions for all to age well today and into the future.** The COO develops leaders, strengthens systems, fosters collaboration and innovation, and ensures that NCOA’s operations remain aligned with its values, strategy, and commitment to measurable social impact.

**COMPETENCIES AND EXPECTATIONS**

* **Strategic Thinking** - Develops strategies to achieve organizational goals; understands organization's strengths & weaknesses; analyzes market and competition; identifies external threats and opportunities; adapts strategy to changing conditions.

* **Judgment** - Displays willingness to make decisions; exhibits sound and accurate judgment; supports and explains reasoning for decisions; includes appropriate people in decision-making process; makes timely decisions.
* **Planning/Organizing** - Prioritizes and plans work activities; uses time efficiently; plans for additional resources; sets goals and objectives; organizes or schedules other people and their tasks; develops realistic action plans.
* **Professionalism** - Approaches others in a tactful manner; reacts well under pressure; treats others with respect and consideration regardless of their status or position; accepts responsibility for own actions; follows through on commitments.
* **Adaptability** - Adapts to changes in the work environment; manages competing demands; changes approach or method to best fit the situation; able to deal with frequent change, delays, or unexpected events.

* Lead and integrate core operational functions including information technology, human resources, compliance, finance and administration.

* Partner with the CEO and senior leadership to drive the execution of NCOA’s strategic plan.

* Identify organizational risks and opportunities and implement strategies to strengthen resilience and scalability.

* Foster a culture of continuous improvement and innovation across operations, people systems, and technology, using data analytics and operational insights to enhance effectiveness and efficiency
* Leverage data, technology, and process improvements to enhance efficiency and effectiveness.
* Drive Artificial Intelligence (AI) enablement across the organization.

**Job Overview**

www.aleet.app

**About ALEET**

ALEET is a private-driver platform built around pre-booked transportation, driver continuity, multi-stop service, and a higher level of coordination than traditional rideshare.

ALEET already has its core platform, operating model, executive structure, Development team, Marketing infrastructure, and chauffeur/provider workflows in place. We are looking for a **Chief Operating Officer (COO) / Cofounder** to own the Operations Unit and oversee the human operating layer of the company.

**The Role**

The COO will own and oversee:

* Chauffeur and provider onboarding and coordination
* Provider readiness and ongoing communication
* Customer support and service issues requiring human judgment
* Customer and provider exceptions and escalations
* Day-to-day service operations
* Operations talent and future operational scaling
* Oversight of automated workflows where human decisions are required
* Coordination with the CEO, CTO, CMO, and executive leadership

This is not a role where someone is being asked to build the operating model from scratch. ALEET’s core systems and structure are already in place. The COO takes ownership of Operations and ensures that service, providers, customers, and operational workflows function effectively as the company grows.

**Who We’re Looking For**

We are looking for someone with real management and operational experience. You do not need to have previously held the title of COO. Strong candidates may come from operations management, general management, regional management, customer operations, transportation, hospitality, logistics, or another environment where they have been responsible for people, service, and day-to-day execution.

The right person should be comfortable making decisions, managing people, solving operational problems, communicating directly with customers and providers when necessary, and taking responsibility for an entire operating function.

**Compensation & Executive Economics**

Starting compensation: **$150,000 per year.**

ALEET operates through Principal Units, with the COO responsible for the Operations Unit. The Operations Unit participates in **25% of ALEET’s quarterly Distributable Profit** under the company’s executive economic structure.

Long-term equity is earned separately based on lasting contribution and documented performance, with an executive equity cap of up to **25%**.

**Work Structure**

Remote within the United States.

This is a senior operating position with direct responsibility for ALEET’s Operations Unit and participation in the company’s executive leadership.

Pay: From $84,000.00 per year

Work Location: Remote

jobs.title: Deputy Director, TB Delivery
jobs.description:
**The Foundation**

We are the largest nonprofit fighting poverty, disease, and inequity around the world. Founded on a simple premise: people everywhere, regardless of identity or circumstances, should have the chance to live healthy, productive lives. We believe our employees should reflect the rich diversity of the global populations we aim to serve. We provide an exceptional benefits package to employees and their families which include comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage with no premiums, generous paid time off, paid family leave, foundation-paid retirement contribution, regional holidays, and opportunities to engage in several employee communities. As a workplace, we’re committed to creating an environment for you to thrive both personally and professionally.

**The Team**

Our Global Health (GH) division harnesses advances in science and technology to save lives in poor countries. We focus on the health problems that have a major impact in developing countries but get too little attention and funding. Where tools exist, we support sustainable ways to improve their delivery. Where they don’t, we invest in research and development of new interventions, such as vaccines, drugs, and diagnostics. Our work in infectious diseases focuses on strategies to fight and prevent HIV/AIDS, malaria, tuberculosis (TB), neglected tropical diseases, enteric and diarrheal diseases, pneumonia and maternal, newborn and child health.  
  
Our TB and HIV work is combined under a joint TB/HIV Program Strategy Team (PST) which focuses on research, development and delivery of new products and tools. The foundation’s Tuberculosis (TB) team aims to address key gaps along the TB care pathway through new approaches to protecting against infection, preventing progression from infection to disease, and improving diagnosis and treatment. Our efforts are diversified based on the understanding that vaccines, diagnostics, drugs, and innovative healthcare delivery are all essential to addressing the TB epidemic. Planning and introducing these new tools will be central to our activities.  
  
We focus our HIV efforts on some of the countries hardest hit by HIV in sub-Saharan Africa, particularly in populations at greatest risk of infection, including adolescent girls and young women. While treatment scale-up has led to significant declines in new infections and mortality, the rate is not rapid enough to reach globally agreed targets and there remains a persistently high incidence and mortality in several countries in SSA. The HIV team’s strategic vision is to accelerate the reduction in the incidence of HIV infection in high-burden geographies and populations, with a focus on the development of new and affordable prevention and treatment interventions, including long-acting drugs, vaccines and biologics, and to enable their effective use.

**Your Role**

The TB&HIV Delivery Team is recruiting a Deputy Director, TB Delivery, who will support the Director, HIV & TB Delivery and Program Strategy team (PST) in achieving its impact goals by supporting the development and implementation of the foundation’s HIV & TB Delivery portfolio. As the Deputy Director, you will report to the Director, HIV & TB Delivery and will integrate with key technical/functional colleagues within the team and across the matrix (across teams). Responsibilities will include managing the execution of a growing and complex portfolio of investments in HIV & TB Delivery and focus on strengthening partnerships with global health institutions to meet the PST’s strategic objectives. You will work to also entail building the capability of the PST to ensure impact across the HIV & TB Delivery portfolio. You will own the management, integration, & oversight of portfolios of foundation investments (grants and contracts) through a highly matrixed organization while also working with external partners to drive progress toward our goals. You will participate in cross Global Health efforts to enhance our integration, accelerate impact, and maintain a cohesive and dynamic culture.

**What You’ll Do**

* Be accountable for innovations in designing and implementing strategies to assist our focus countries to reduce TB incidence and mortality
* Work with members of the TB delivery team and assist them to plan and execute their strategies with fidelity
* Work with the team to plan and implement new technologies e.g., diagnostics, therapeutics and vaccines as they come on stream
* Provide strategic guidance in crafting grants and contracts that require research, modeling and analytics
* Facilitate development of annual and multiyear investment plans and budgets, develop and modify and implement strategies under the leadership of the Director
* Lead partnerships with internal and external partners and grantees to advance the foundation’s priorities for TB
* Accountable for the identification and assessment of key portfolio risks and the development and management of mitigation plans
* Work with foundation leadership as requested to address cross-cutting issues and improve functions and performance
* Advise, mentor and support colleagues within the TB Delivery team and their grantees in the design, enhancement and execution of the innovation for delivery strategy
* Participate in and learn from the program strategy and other teams, practice Diversity, Equity & Inclusion (DEI) efforts to ensure that we are continuing to make progress towards realizing our commitments.
* Ability to travel 30% domestically and internationally.

**Investment Relationship and Management**

* Identify promising areas of implementation science research and innovation to fill key gaps in our knowledge of the interventions needed for more rapidly reducing the burden of TB as well as develop and/or guide the development of related Requests for Proposals (RFPs) and specific proposals.
* Provide strategic guidance in crafting grants and contracts that require complex research or analyt

jobs.title: Executive Director Memory Care
jobs.description:
**Frontier Senior Living** is seeking an experienced **Executive Director** to manage the day-to-day operations of the **Catalina Springs Memory Care** community located in **Oro Valley, AZ**. Demonstrated success as a leader in similar settings is required of the Executive Director.

**This position requires that applicants have an active and in-good-standing Assisted Living Facility Manager Certification in the State of Arizona.**

***Position qualifies for Performance Based Bonus Programs! See below for more detail.***

Frontier Senior Living's portfolio of communities spans throughout the United States with each community sharing a commitment to superior service and quality lifestyle for our residents within their own unique setting. Frontier's mission is to provide an enriched and meaningful experience for our residents, team members, and community partners. If you are as committed and passionate about serving the needs of our senior residents as we are, we encourage you to apply and experience the Frontier Difference.

The **Executive Director** will be responsible for managing the day-to-day operations of all departments within the community. This includes achieving and maintaining maximum occupancy of the community while focusing on high resident satisfaction and quality resident care/services. The Executive Director will ensure compliance with applicable state and federal requirements and ensure a smooth operation of the community through staff development and employee satisfaction.

**Primary Duties and Responsibilities:**

* Ensures the delivery of quality care and services and promotes positive resident and family relations, responding promptly and appropriately to resident needs, requests and concerns. Encourages resident interaction and promotes a culture where each resident is of the greatest importance
* Operates the community in a manner which will ensure company profitability by meeting all community budget and census guidelines as set by Corporate
* Directs and monitors all marketing activities to achieve a 100% occupied community
* Provides resident programs designed to provide enrichment in the areas of social interaction, entertainment, arts and crafts, physical exercise, education, religious services, and community involvement
* Complies with all state and federal laws and regulations and all company rules and regulations regarding the care of the residents and operation of the community. Develops a positive rapport with all state regulatory representatives
* Oversees the healthcare related programs and services (i.e. medications, bathing, staff development, charting) and ensures that all applicable state-mandated rules and regulations are carefully adhered to
* Directs and monitors timely and accurate completion of all daily/weekly/monthly billings, accounting and bookkeeping requirements
* Assists as needed in the coordination of move-in with respective residents. Periodically reviews each resident’s status and ability to perform under the terms and conditions of the Residency Agreement
* Actively manages and leads the community team, including recruiting and retention of key contributors, performance management, employee development, coaching, and feedback
* Routinely monitors the sanitation of the kitchen, quality of meals, quantity, and appearance of service and entire staff, cleanliness of resident apartment and satisfaction of residents
* Implement a quality assurance program that evaluates each department’s performance on an on-going basis
* Provides a safe environment for residents, staff, and visitors
* Performs additional duties as assigned to ensure business continuity

The **Executive Director** qualifies for **Performance Based Bonus Programs**! Frontier Senior Living has two established Performance Based Bonus programs for our community’s Management team: **The Exceeding Net Operating Income Bonus and the Marketing Bonus Program (Management Team)**. It is the goal of Frontier Senior Living to award its employees for diligent efforts and outcomes which positively impact the Company and its future, including striving to control costs, maintaining high levels of resident satisfaction and reaching high census targets.

jobs.title: Executive Director, QCORE
jobs.description:
The Executive Director of QCORE serves as the head of a university-wide research institute and works closely with affiliated faculty and staff to build and lead a successful program advancing research and scientific discovery in quantum science, engineering, and business.  
  
QCORE’s primary objective is to empower Montana’s quantum ecosystem by uniting cutting-edge research, industry partnerships, and community engagement – enabling breakthrough technologies that shape the future of quantum innovation. The vision of QCORE is to lead Montana’s transformation into a global powerhouse for quantum-enabled technologies by 2035, fostering economic growth, academic excellence and a resilient, future-focused workforce.  
  
QCORE exists to steward the development of transformative quantum technologies in service to the common good. QCORE will help students plan for careers in quantum and quantum-enabling systems and will support transitioning into those careers through strategic partnerships with Montana’s growing quantum industry. Strategic partnerships serve as the mechanism for QCORE to strengthen relationships between industry, research and innovators – growing collaboration and creating shared opportunities for beneficial technology innovations.  
  
Pending approval of research center status, QCORE is housed in The College of Letters & Science (CLS), the largest center for learning, teaching and research at Montana State University. CLS offers students an excellent liberal arts and sciences education in nearly 50 majors, 25 minors and over 25 graduate degrees within the four areas of the humanities, natural sciences, mathematical, and social sciences.  
  
Building on the great strength of our traditional disciplines, the college provides exciting opportunities for faculty and students at the cutting edge of interdisciplinary inquiry. CLS is dedicated to supporting student success, discovering and disseminating new knowledge, and providing an atmosphere in which discovery and learning are integrated and valued. CLS is at the confluence of intellectual tradition, discovery, and innovation.  
  
When research center status is finalized for QCORE, the center will be in the Office of the Vice President for Research and Economic Development.

  

**Duties and Responsibilities**

* Strategically position QCORE to be a nationally recognized, best-in-class research and development center for advancement of quantum technology, a leader in quantum workforce development and a deeply integrated innovation ecosystem that supports the translation of quantum and related technologies to industry.
* Develop and implement long-term strategies to improve QCORE’s overall sustainability, effectiveness, and responsiveness to the needs of sponsoring organizations and companies in the state, region, nation, and internationally.
* Develop and maintain a best-in-class governance structure for QCORE.
* Build and nurture long-term relationships with key stakeholders, including federal agencies, individual donors, institutional funders, congressional representatives, and corporate partners.
* Build strategic alliances and partnerships with other testbeds, academic institutions, corporations, and governments to expand QCORE’s reach, visibility, and impact.
* Lead efforts to secure sustainable funding through partnerships, campaigns, and new initiatives to diversify the organization’s revenue (e.g., federal and private grants, federal cooperative awards, donations, industrial partnerships, social enterprises). This includes engagement with our legislature.
* Participate in sector-specific organizations relevant to quantum technologies and quantum supply chain, including standards development and testbed communities of practice. Present at national and international gatherings of experts in these respective fields.
* Leads efforts to ensure that QCORE remains a vital part of MSU’s land-grant mission, promoting quantum science and economic development in Montana, the region, and nation, and providing practical learning opportunities for students.
* Support QCORE faculty and scientists seeking and obtaining external funding to promote innovation, discovery, and dissemination of quantum science and technology.
* Ensure operational excellence, overseeing all aspects of budgeting, accounting, personnel, facilities, security, and safety.
* Ensure that QCORE complies with all legal, regulatory, safety, and ethical standards at local, national, and international levels.
* Ensure that QCORE meets all required grant reporting requirements.
* Coordinate with QCORE’s leadership team to lead and mentor staff, fostering a positive, collaborative, and mission-driven organizational culture.
* Oversee the monitoring and evaluation of program outcomes to measure success and inform future strategies at a national and international level.
* Prioritize sustainability in all programs and initiatives, ensuring long-term environmental, social, and financial viability.

  

**Required Qualifications – Experience, Education, Knowledge & Skills**

* PhD in Physics, Engineering, or a related field, or a terminal degree with equivalent industry experience.

* Demonstrated experience in strategic leadership of a research center or related entity, or business.

* Demonstrated experience in federal research grant-seeking, fundraising, or business development.

  

**Preferred Qualifications – Experience, Education, Knowledge & Skills**

* Demonstrated experience with technology transfer.

jobs.title: Corps Director of Development I
jobs.description:
**LOCATION:** Salisbury, Maryland Corps

**POSITION:** Corps Director of Development I

**POSITION TYPE:** full-time, exempt

**PAY RATE:** $61,000 - $65,000

**This position is responsible for:**

Creating and overseeing the implementation of a strategic approach to increase fundraising results through major gifts, corporate donations, grant solicitation, direct mail, special events, community relations and in-kind resources.

**Key Responsibilities:**

**ANNUAL FUND DEVELOPMENT ACTIVITIES**

* By February 15th each year create a fund development plan in consultation with the Corps Officer and Divisional Development Director (DDD) that includes an individual goal for the development director and sets specific goals and strategies for appropriate development disciplines that will increase revenues to support the strategic direction of the organization; plan is submitted to the Corps Officer for approval and processing though the DDD for DFB for approval. Implement the approved fund development plan in accordance with ethical fundraising principles.
* By the 15th of each month, evaluate and report to the Corps Officer on all fundraising activities to ensure that the fundraising goals are being achieved.
* In collaboration with the Corps Officer develop and maintain the Community Relations & Development Committee, the Marketing and Public Relations Committee and the Bequest and Endowment Committee of the Advisory Board.
* Actively support and cooperate with the divisional Planned Giving and Resource Development program representatives.
* Monitor trends in the community or region and adapt fundraising strategies as necessary.
* Cultivate existing funding resources and research and secure new funding opportunities for the command.
* Manage and provide oversight over the three (3) major annual fundraising events (Golf tournament, Annual Dinner, and Kettle breakfast).

**ORGANIZE FUND DEVELOPMENT ACTIVITIES**

* Develop and manage timelines for various fundraising activities to ensure strategic plans and critical fund-raising processes are carried out in a timely manner.
* Develop procedures for the development department which reflect ethical fundraising practices.
* Prepare and submit grant applications as outlined in the development plan.
* Oversee the planning and execution of special fundraising events as specified in the development plan.
* In cooperation with the Regional Resource Development Director and Corps Officer, identify and develop a personal portfolio of at least 20 corporate, community and/or individual prospects that will be put into a moves management system that the development director manages.
* Meet or surpass an annual fundraising goal from major gift efforts that is established by the Corps Officer and approved by the Divisional Finance Board.
* In cooperation with the Regional Resource Development Director, manage a portfolio of the top 10 prospects and donors for the Corps Officer’s involvement.
* In cooperation with the Regional Planned Giving Director staff the Bequest and Endowment Committee of the Advisory Board.
* Increase overall revenue on an annual basis as established in the annual fund-raising plan.
* Oversee the administration of a donor mailing list and Inter-Change which respects the privacy and confidentiality of donor information.
* Work with direct mail vendors on all aspects of direct mail, set up annual calendar of mailings, review appeals and ensure timely processing of approvals from the Corps Officer, provide monthly direct mail reports and provide analysis on the direct mail program.
* Have a strong working knowledge of InterChange, personally enter the recording of all gifts and donor interactions in a timely and proper manner.
* Manages the acknowledgement program to provide a high level of donor relations.
* Coordinate in-kind donations and make decisions regarding the issuing of receipts.
* Manage the United Way application process and follow up processes according to policy.

**STAFF FUND DEVELOPMENT ACTIVITIES**

* Engage volunteers for special fund development projects using established volunteer management practices.
* Assist the Corps Officer in staffing the Advisory Organizations.

**MANAGE FUND DEVELOPMENT BUDGET**

* By February 15th each year develop and submit to the Corps Officer an annual revenue and expenditure budget for the fund development program.
* Monitor expenses and analyze budget reports on fund development and recommend changes as necessary.

**PUBLIC RELATIONS**

* Foster an understanding of philanthropy within the organization.
* Develop a comprehensive communication and marketing plan to promote the organization and maximize public awareness of the fundraising activities of the organization and of the value of Family Thrift Store.
* Coordinate the design, printing and distribution of marketing and communication materials for development efforts in accordance with the communications and marketing plan.
* Produce an annual report by February 15th of each year.
* Build relationships with community stakeholders to advance the mission and fundraising goals of the organization.
* Produce and distribute a minimum of 12 press releases in accordance with the communications and marketing plan.
* Manage the Corps website and social media program.

**PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS AND WORKING CONDITIONS**

* Limited amount of physical effort required associated with walking, standing, lifting, and carrying light objects (less than 25 lbs.).
* Work may be performed in an office environment where there are little or no physical discomforts associated with changes in weather or discomforts associated with noise, dust, dirt, and the like but not limited to the office environment.

**Employee Benefits:**

* Paid Time Off
* Retirement Savings Plan Available
* Supplemental Insurance Available
* Voluntary Life Insurance and more!

**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS REQUIRED**

**EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE**

* Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college

jobs.description:
**Introduction**
----------------

The Deputy Director of Tourism & Events serves as a key operational leader, providing day-to-day management of the department and oversight of the City’s major tourism and cultural contracts. Reporting directly to the Senior Director, this role is responsible for ensuring consistent execution, performance accountability, and alignment with the City’s strategic priorities. This position is central to the effective administration of Scottsdale’s tourism and events portfolio. The Deputy Director oversees the City’s relationships with its contracted partners, including Experience Scottsdale and Scottsdale Arts, ensuring contractual obligations are met, performance is monitored, and issues are identified and addressed proactively.
  
While the Senior Director serves as the City’s primary strategic and external-facing leader, the Deputy Director ensures that departmental operations, contract administration, and team performance are executed with consistency, discipline, and attention to detail. This role requires a highly organized and thoughtful professional who can translate policy and agreements into day-to-day operations, manage competing priorities, and support a high-performing, accountable team environment.
